overview: Black declines the pawn with ...c6 and keeps a solid Slav-like centre, so White's g4 push has gained little and weakened the kingside. White follows with h3, d3 or c4 and tries to catch up in development, while Black gets a comfortable game with ...e5 or ...Bxg4 later. White's king is slightly exposed and the position is easier for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto on the long diagonal, then h3, d3 and c4
Hope Black overreaches and enter a flexible set-up

black_ideas.idea: Take a solid centre with ...c6, ...e5 and ...Nf6
Pick off the weakened g4 pawn later if White errs

typical_structures.structure: Black Slav-type d5/c6 centre against White's g4 and long-diagonal bishop

character.notes: Quirky, not forcing; White has loosened the kingside but Black has no clear attack.

gambit.notes: Declined: the g4 pawn is not taken, so no material has changed hands.

soundness.notes: Slightly inferior for White but not refuted; Short played it.

structure.notes: Flank opening; the centre stays flexible.

level.notes: Little theory; White's position is hard to justify.

sublines_that_differ.name: Grob Gambit accepted
sublines_that_differ.how: Not this root; White gives a pawn for development and the long diagonal

character.reason: Quirky flank play without forced tactics.

gambit.reason: The pawn was not taken so no material is offered here.

soundness.reason: Slightly worse for White but not refuted.

structure.reason: Flank opening with an undecided centre.

approach.reason: The Grob is anchored as offbeat.

level.reason: Little theory but not a good first repertoire choice.

plans.reason: White's bishop on g2 on the long diagonal.
